The protection mechanism against decompression bombs fails to mitigate the brotli variant, allowing remote servers to crash clients with less than 80GB of available memory. This occurs because brotli can achieve extremely high compression ratios for zero-filled data, leading to excessive memory consumption during decompression. Mitigation for this v

expect.note: httpx 0.24.1 (requirements.txt httpx[http2]==0.24.1, Brotli==1.1.0) auto-decodes Content-Encoding: br via brotli.Decompressor when brotli is installed and adds 'br' to default Accept-Encoding. Engine requests (searx/network/network.py request -> response .text/.content) fully decode responses from external engine servers (attacker-influenced), with no decompressed-size cap in brotli 1.1.0 -> brotli bomb memory DoS. Some engines even request br explicitly (searx/engines/tineye.py:74). Image proxy uses aiter_raw (searx/network/__init__.py:197-199) so it is not a path, but engine fetches are.

facts.advisory_summary: Certifi is a curated collection of Root Certificates for validating the trustworthiness of SSL certificates while verifying the identity of TLS hosts. Certifi starting in 2021.05.30 and prior to 2024.07.4 recognized root certificates from `GLOBALTRUST`. Certifi 2024.07.04 removes root certificates from `GLOBALTRUST` from the root store. These are in the process of being removed from Mozilla's trust store. `GLOBALTRUST`'s root certificates are being removed pursuant to an investigation which identified "long-running and unresolved compliance issues."

expect.note: All outgoing engine TLS uses httpx.create_ssl_context(cert, verify=True, trust_env) (searx/network/client.py:54-59,127,145; verify defaults True network.py:65), which in httpx loads certifi.where() unless SSL_CERT_FILE is set (not set in repo/dockerfiles). So the GLOBALTRUST roots in certifi 2024.6.2 are trusted for engine/image-proxy connections; exploitation needs an on-path attacker with a mis-issued cert.

facts.advisory_summary:
certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys — Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them.

expect.note: Same trust path as row 1: searx/network/client.py:57 httpx.create_ssl_context(verify=True) -> certifi bundle (2024.6.2 includes emSign ECC Root CA - G3). On-path attacker with a compromised eMudhra intermediate key could MITM engine responses that SearXNG parses and renders.

facts.advisory_summary:
Jinja2 vulnerable to sandbox breakout through attr filter selecting format method — An oversight in how the Jinja sandboxed environment interacts with the `|attr` filter allows an attacker that controls the content of a template to execute arbitrary Python code.

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker needs to control the content of a template. Whether that is the case depends on the type of application using Jinja. This vulnerability impacts users of applications which execute untrusted templates.

Jinja's sandbox does catch calls to `str.format` and ensures they don't escape the sandbox.

expect.note: No SandboxedEnvironment anywhere in searx; templates are trusted repo files (Flask app.jinja_env, searx/webapp.py:163). The only from_string is searx/infopage/__init__.py:70 on bundled infopage markdown files (read from disk, :60-64), not user input. Attacker never controls template content.

facts.advisory_summary:
Jinja has a sandbox breakout through malicious filenames — A bug in the Jinja compiler allows an attacker that controls both the content and filename of a template to execute arbitrary Python code, regardless of if Jinja's sandbox is used.

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker needs to control both the filename and the contents of a template. Whether that is the case depends on the type of application using Jinja. This vulnerability impacts users of applications which execute untrusted templates where the template author can also choose the template filename.

expect.note: Requires attacker control of both template filename and content. SearXNG templates come from searx/templates and bundled infopage files (searx/infopage/__init__.py:60-70); no user-supplied template names/contents.

facts.advisory_summary:
lxml: Default configuration of iterparse() and ETCompatXMLParser() allows XXE to local files — ### Impact
Using either of the two parsers in the default configuration (with `resolve_entities=True`) allows untrusted XML input to read local files.

### Patches
lxml 6.1.0 changes the default to `resolve_entities='internal'`, thus disallowing local file access by default.

### Workarounds
Setting the `resolve_entities` option explicitly to `resolve_entities='internal'` or `resolve_entities=False` disables the local file access.

### Resources
Original report: https://bugs.launchpad.net/lxml/+bug/2

expect.note: grep for iterparse/ETCompatXMLParser/XMLParser/resolve_entities in searx/ returns nothing; engines parse via lxml.html.fromstring / etree.fromstring/XPath only, not the two affected parsers. No dependency in requirements.txt calls them either.

facts.advisory_summary: Pygments has Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) due to Inefficient Regex for GUID Matching — A security flaw has been discovered in pygments before 2.20.0. The impacted element is the function AdlLexer of the file pygments/lexers/archetype.py. The manipulation results in inefficient regular expression complexity. The attack is only possible with local access. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

expect.note: Code results are highlighted with pygments: searx/templates/simple/result_templates/code.html:28 -> code_highlighter (searx/webapp.py:209-216) calls get_lexer_by_name(result.code_language). searchcode_code engine sets code_language to the file extension from searchcode.com's JSON (searx/engines/searchcode_code.py:59-71), so a file '*.adl' selects AdlLexer (pygments 2.18.0 lexers/archetype.py:249-256, nested-quantifier archetype_id regex :37-40) on externally-sourced code lines. Engine is disabled: true by default (settings.yml:1633-1636) but any visitor can enable it in preferences on a default instance; ReDoS impact plausibility unverified.
